subject: Supplier Crypto Key Handling & Subprocessor Ownership Reconciliation
messages:
From: Ella Pruitt <ella.pruitt@carewellhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@carewellhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: reconciliation of subprocessor key custody + SIG evidence

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of CareWell's vendor intake we need to reconcile a couple of items tied to crypto key custody and downstream subprocessor ownership for SOC 2 / SIG scoping. Specific asks: 

- A current roster of all subprocessors that have any ability to access encrypted customer data (direct or via KMS).
- Which subprocessors hold any persistent keys, sign/verify keys, or long-term key custody versus transient/ephemeral key access.
- KMS pathing diagram and a short statement of operational controls (rotation, least privilege, split knowledge if applicable).
- Any CAIQ / SIG reference where these ownerships are already documented (we can accept an exported workbook).

Would you be able to provide the roster and a short reconciliation note by EOD Monday? Our security team will attach this to the vendor risk record (Vendor ID: CW-3392).

Best,
Ella Pruitt
Information Security Manager
CareWell Health

---

P.S. If there are narrow limitations (e.g., certain on-prem private deployments), call them out — we can scope accordingly.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ella Pruitt <ella.pruitt@carewellhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: reconciliation of subprocessor key custody + SIG evidence

Hi Ella — thanks for the clear list. Summary and action plan below.

Quick answers up front:
- We'll attach a current subprocessor roster CSV and a short evidence workbook for SIG/CAIQ mapping.
- Redwood does not hand over long-term customer master keys to third parties. Subprocessors typically get ephemeral tokens or are routed through our KMS proxy when performing inference-only tasks.

Action plan (timeline):
1) I will upload a snapshot CSV (subprocessor_roster_snapshot.csv) with fields: name, role, access_type (kms_proxy / direct_kms / telemetry_only), last_attestation_date.
2) Laura will add the KMS pathing diagram and an operational controls summary (rotation, access reviews, split roles).
3) Monica will add the SIG/CAIQ worksheet with exact question mappings we use in our SOC2 pack.

We aim to get the files to you by EOD Monday the 24th. If you need an interim note or a short call to walk the diagram, happy to schedule.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Security Partnerships (sales-security liaison)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: reconciliation of subprocessor key custody + SIG evidence

Hi all — attaching the KMS pathing diagram (kms_pathing_diagram.pdf) and a short controls note. Key points to call out for your risk team: 

- Master keys (customer CMKs) are tenant-scoped and managed inside our customer KMS layer; we do not export raw customer keys to subprocessors.
- Subprocessors that perform model inference receive ephemeral signing tokens via our token broker that are scoped and TTL-limited (default 5 minutes).
- A small set of operational vendors (e.g., EdgeServe Inc.) have read-only telemetry hooks that ingest anonymized usage telemetry; they do not receive any key material.
- Key rotation and access reviews: we rotate internal service keys on a 90-day cadence, and customer-facing CMKs are rotated per customer or per request; rotation events are logged and retained in audit trail for 1 year (longer retention available as enterprise add-on).

If CareWell requires split-knowledge or HSM attestations for a particular deployment, flag that and we can detail the private deployment options and associated documentation.

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms_pathing_diagram.pdf

Ella / Ben — attaching the requested evidence workbook (carewell_sig_submission.xlsx) and the roster snapshot (subprocessor_roster_snapshot.csv). High-level notes included in the workbook tab "recon_notes":

- EdgeServe Inc. listed as telemetry_only; they receive anonymized usage metrics and do not touch request payloads or key material. EdgeServe completed our vendor security intake on 2026-08-15 (attestation on file).
- Model hosting partners (listed as kms_proxy) never persist customer keys; they call our KMS proxy with an ephemeral session token and never store secret material.
- A single third party (KeyVault Partners) manages HSM-backed signing for our release pipeline; they hold split-key escrow for code-signing only, not customer data encryption.

Files attached: subprocessor_roster_snapshot.csv, carewell_sig_submission.xlsx

Next steps: if you want a short call to walk the KMS diagram and the workbook mappings to CAIQ controls, we have availability tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Redwood Inference
